source_title: Patrick Stewart’s Star Trek Family, Including William Shatner, Mourn the Icon: ‘Captain Picard Stood for the Best of Us’ - People.com
source_excerpt:
The prolific actor played Jean-Luc Picard across multiple films and series in the franchise, beginning with ‘Star Trek: The Next Generation’
Patrick Stewart died on Wednesday, Oct. 28, at age 86
Known for his work across multiple franchises, the prolific actor played Captain Picard in the Star Trek universe, notably Star Trek: The Next Generation
Castmates remembered Stewart with tributes on Thursday, Oct. 29 after a spokesperson announced his death
Patrick Stewart ’s Star Trek castmates are remembering their captain.
On Thursday, Oct. 29, a spokesperson for the prolific actor — who played Jean-Luc Picard across multiple films and series in the franchise — confirmed that he died on Wednesday, Oct. 28 in Los Angeles .
Stewart had played Picard since the debut of Star Trek: The Next Generation in 1987, and reprised the role multiple times after the show’s seven-season run. His final performance as the character came in Star Trek: Picard , which ran from 2020 to 2023. Several of Stewart’s Star Trek castmates and other members of the franchise paid tribute to him following his death.
Among those who paid honored him was William Shatner , 95, who appeared alongside Stewart in 1994’s Star Trek Generations .
“What a heartbreaking week it has been,” Shatner began, referring to Walter Koenig , an original star of the series who died at age 90 on Oct. 25. “Sir Patrick Stewart was a friend, a colleague, and a magnificent actor. From the stage to the bridge of the Enterprise, he brought intelligence, grace, and a deep sense of humanity to everything he did. Captain Picard stood for the best of us, and so did the man who played him. I was filled with affection and admiration for him and his work.”
He added, “My heart goes out to Sunny and his family. He will be deeply missed.”
George Takei also shared a tribute on Thursday, remembering Stewart as a man who “inspired a whole next generation of star-gazers.” “Fans across the world mourn the passing of a true and irreplaceable legend. As Captain Jean-Luc Picard, Patrick Stewart took the starship Enterprise to places it had never gone before,” he wrote on Bluesky . “He inspired a whole next generation of star-gazers who looked longingly ahead to a brighter future for all humanity. Our hearts are heavy, indeed. Rest in the heavens, Captain.” Wil Wheaton, who appeared alongside Stewart on The Next Generation , shared a photo of them on Instagram alongside the message, “Godspeed, Captain.”
Rebecca Romijn , who starred in Star Trek: Strange New Worlds and the X-Men franchise alongside Stewart, shared a tribute on Instagram alongside the message, “What a gift to have been your friend. Rest in peace, dear Patrick.”
“I feel so grateful to have known him for the last 25 years and to have been in his orbit for that last 25 years, both as a fellow mutant and as a fellow member of Starfleet,” she began. “He was positively delicious, hilarious, naughty, incredible sense of humor.”
Romijn remembered “that booming voice of his, that always spoke to the very back of the room, as every classically trained Shakespearean great needs to master,” adding Stewart “has always been an inspiration.”
She concluded, “I want to send my condolences to his family. I’ll miss my friend dearly. Rest in peace, Patrick.”
Stewart first made his mark as Picard in The Next Generation , which also starred LeVar Burton , Jonathan Frakes , Michael Dorn, Marina Sirtis, Brent Spiner and Gates McFadden, among others. The sci-fi series ran for 178 episodes through seven seasons, through 1994.
After The Next Generation wrapped, Stewart reprised the role for four Star Trek films from 1994 to 2002, before returning to TV screens as Picard in the Paramount+ series Star Trek: Picard in 2020. Picard ran for three seasons until 2023, and also starred Alison Pill, Isa Briones , Jeri Ryan and Michelle Hurd, among others. Several The Next Generation cast members also returned for the show to reprise their roles decades later.
In a statement shared with Variety , Akiva Goldsman, co-showrunner and co-creator of Star Trek: Picard , wrote that Stewart was “not only a true lion of the profession, he was the rarest of alchemists, one who could literally turn the written word into flesh and blood.”
“Patrick was kind, strong, fiercely intelligent, collaborative, vulnerable and wise. His Captain Jean-Luc Picard permanently expanded the universe of Star Trek without measure. He will be deeply missed by this one fan and by so many more.”
Speaking with PEOPLE in 2023, Stewart said that he initially didn’t have plans to reunite with his former castmates when signing on for Picard . “Initially, my feeling had been — I had certain conditions attached to signing onto this. Though I was excited about the idea of a Star Trek series called Picard , Next Generation was something I thought we had done great work on, but this now was something very different,” he said. “So even when we started shooting, there wasn’t a plan about the assembly.”
He added, “But then in season 1, I played one scene with Marina Sirtis and Jonathan as Riker. And little by little I saw that I had been wrong to put a veto on full TNG cast elements in this new series. And I think that it’s worked out to everyone’s satisfaction. I know I enjoyed it immensely.”
In July, Stewart spoke with TV Insider about his connection to the role and the many franchise anniversaries approaching, including the 40th anniversary of The Next Generation . “All of these anniversaries are wildly surreal for me, but the 40th anniversary of The Next Generation is particularly remarkable. I still remember my first day driving onto the Paramount lot like it was yesterday,” he said.
Stewart also spoke on how Picard’s story ended. “The final scene of The Next Generation [the episode “All Good Things…”] has always felt like such a beautiful send-off, but of course we then filmed multiple movies after the series wrapped,” he said. “I truly thought Nemesis was my last time playing Jean-Luc, but then along came Picard — and I’m delighted with how that series ended.”
On Thursday, a spokesperson for Stewart confirmed his death and noted that he died “in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia.”
“He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all,” the statement from Kelly Bush Novak read. “We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace.”
